canonical_topic: Barrel of oil equivalent (BOE) and tonne of oil equivalent (TOE) conversions
definition: Standard approximate conversion factors used to express reserves of different fuel types (oil, natural gas, etc.) in a single common unit, the barrel of oil equivalent (BOE) or tonne of oil equivalent (TOE), since some fuels (e.g., methane, propane) exist as gas and must be normalized against oil-equivalent units for aggregate reserve reporting.
core_idea: BOE/TOE are standardized energy-equivalent units that let reserves of oil and gas be added together and reported as one aggregate figure, commonly expressed at the billion-barrel (BBOE) scale.
key_points: 1 billion barrels of oil equivalent is abbreviated 1 BBOE.
Fossil fuel reserves are commonly reported in BOE (or TOE) units so different fuel types can be aggregated.
Natural gas reserves are converted into BOE using approximate energy/volume equivalence factors.
relationships: Used alongside proven/probable/possible reserve classification for aggregate reserve reporting
